name: Every Proper Ample Family Contains Opposite Equal Maximum Fibres
statement: Let $\varnothing\ne H\subsetneq Q_E$ be ample and form its antipodal double $\widehat H=(\{0\}\times H)\cup(\{1\}\times\overline H)$. There are $R\subseteq E$ and $f\in Q_R$ such that the opposite conditionings agree, $H_f=H_{\overline f}=:A$, the common fibre $A$ is a pseudogeometric maximum class, and $(\{0\}\times A)\cup(\{1\}\times\overline A)$ is minimal nonample. One may take $R=\varnothing$ exactly when $\widehat H$ is minimal nonample. If $r=|R|>0$, then $(r+1)|A|\le|H|$, with equality exactly when $H=A\times P$ for one antipodal geodesic path $P\subseteq Q_R$.
proof: A minimal nonface of the shattered complex of $H$ becomes shattered by $H\cup\overline H$, while every old shattered support occurs both with and without the new layer coordinate. Sauer's inequality therefore makes the antipodal double nonample. Choose a nonample conditioning with minimum remaining dimension. The layer coordinate cannot be fixed, because every conditioning of $H$ or its antipode is ample. The classification of minimal nonample families makes this conditioned double antipodally closed with maximum one-coordinate sections, giving opposite equal fibres $A$ and the pseudogeometric conclusion. For each $a\in A$, its $R$-section in $H$ contains the antipodal words $f,\overline f$ and, by isometry, at least a geodesic of $r+1$ vertices. Summing gives the order bound. Equality forces every such section to be a shortest antipodal path and leaves no vertices over words outside $A$. If two paths ordered some coordinate pair differently, their union would shatter that pair in addition to the $(r+1)|A|$ already forced supports, contradicting Sandwich equality. Hence all paths coincide and $H=A\times P$; conversely this product is ample and attains equality.
comments: The equality characterization is global: ampleness forces the geodesic chosen above every word of the maximum core to be the same path.
